newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker for 3rd straight day.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker for 3rd straight day.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Friday as jittery investors took profits for a third straight session on Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 15.96 points to close at 5706.88 in heavy turnover of 93.8 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.02 million).
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 534 to 408 with 326 issues unchanged.
"The market is biding its time until we hear from the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting next week," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Ketchen said financial markets are not expecting any adjustment in U.S. interest rates following the FOMC meeting on Tuesday.
Although the TSE has dropped about five percent from its peak levels in November, Ketchen said the key index is still up 25 percent on the year.
Other analysts expect the market to resume its climb when money from tax sheltered pension funds begins to flow into the market early next year.
Conglomerates, gold and base metals led 10 of 14 sub-groups lower. Bank stocks topped the gaining column.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. jumped 1.20 to 21 on 8.2 million shares after Indonesia extended the deadline for Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp. to strike a deal to develop the rich Busang gold find to the end of December. Barrick fell 0.70 to 38.80.
* Sherritt International topped the most active list, climbing 0.35 to 50.35 on 9.5 million shares.
* Kyrgoil Corp. fell 0.10 to 1.75 on 4.4 million shares after it updated its joint venture in the Kyrgyz Republic.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd. depressed the conglomerate group, down 0.95 to 33.35 on 800,000 shares.
